questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The toddler decided to make a mess because he wanted to ______ the attention of its parents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word 'seek' is the most appropriate choice
 
• **It means to attempt to find or obtain something.**
 
 
• **It's his job to seek out new customers**
 
 

Therefore, the correct sentence is "The toddler decided to make a mess because he wanted to seek the attention of its parents.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__ **

 
• The other options do not fit the context of the sentence:
 
 
• **Elicit:** This means to draw out a response, answer, or fact from someone, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Please:** This means to make someone happy or satisfied, which is not the toddler's intention in the context given.
 
• **Extract:** This means to remove or take out something, which is not relevant to the context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher assured: “You have completed your homework, __________?”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the question, the teacher is asking for confirmation, which requires a question tag at the end of the sentence.
 
• The main clause is positive (**you have completed**), so the question tag should be** negative.**
 
• Therefore, the correct question tag is "haven't you".

Hence, the correct statement is **"*The teacher assured: “You have completed your homework, haven't you?__”*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Question tags are used to seek confirmation and are generally the opposite form of the main clause (**positive main clause has negative question tag and vice versa).**

 
 
• **Example:** *She is coming, **isn't she?***
 
 
 
• If the main clause is negative, the question tag will be positive.
 
 
• **Example:** *He isn't coming, **is he?***

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Many __a things are__ used for the show.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'Many a things' is** incorrect.**
 
• The correct phrase should be **'Many a thing'** which is singular.
 
• The verb used with 'Many a' should be **singular**.
 
• Therefore, the correct verb form should be 'is' instead of 'are'.

Hence, the correct statement is "*Many a thing **is used** for the show*."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phrase 'Many a' is used in formal English to mean 'a large number of'. It is always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.
 
 
• **Example:** ***Many a student has struggled** with this concept*.
 
 
 
• It is important to remember that despite implying plurality, the noun and verb following 'Many a' should be singular.
 
 
• Example: ***Many a time, he has proven** his worth*.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the __funny__ films of all time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is trying **to convey that the film is renowned for being one of the most humorous films ever made.**
 
• The** correct comparative form** to use in this context should be the superlative form** "funniest"** instead of the positive form** "funny".**
 
• ​When comparing three or more items, we use** the superlative form.**
 
• For adjectives with one or** two syllables, we typically add '-est' to the adjective (e.g., funny → funniest).**
 
• Examples:
 
 
• This is **the most **beautiful garden I have ever seen.
 
• She is** the smartest** student in the class.
 
 

Therefore, the correct statement is** "This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funniest__ films of all time."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **"No rectification needed"** is** incorrect** because the sentence needs a superlative form.
 
• **"More funny"** is** incorrect** because it is not the correct form of comparison.
 
• **"Funnier"** is** incorrect **because it is the comparative form and not the superlative.

• In the context of the given sentence, it justifies the action of distracting his friends by implying that it was acceptable given the circumstances.
